14	CASE OD2-HO-NOCONC-1 (NOCONC, organizational): Two quarters of rising shrink at a mid-size variety store
15	Setting: Marrowby Stores is a fictional regional grocery and general-merchandise chain with 38 stores. Its fiscal year matches the calendar year (Q1 = January–March). Store 14 in Dunmere is a mid-size store with about $2.8 million in quarterly sales. Quarterly shrink figures go to regional leadership. Asset Protection has been asked to review store 14. Today is 10 November FY2026.
16	Presenting request: Regional Director Imelda Charroux wants a plan for store 14 by month-end. Regional Operations needs a decision on the December count by 20 November. Work out what explains the store's rising shrink and recommend what to do next.
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Email from Imelda Charroux, Regional Director (North), 2 Nov (leadership-account): To: Asset Protection. Re: Store 14, Dunmere. Store 14's shrink has climbed two quarters running: 1.5% of sales in Q1, 1.9% in Q2 and 2.3% in Q3, against a chain average of 1.6% in each quarter. That is roughly $24,000 more loss in Q3 than in Q1. Two consecutive rises is a trend, not noise. The four self-checkout lanes went live on 17 March, right before this started, and the vendor's Q3 report shows 412 unscanned-item interventions at the store. Every trade article I read says self-checkout drives shrink. I want a plan by month-end to either pull the lanes or staff them full-time.
19	E2 [stage S1] Interview notes, store manager Dorian Pask, 3 Nov (manager-account): Pask does not think self-checkout is the issue. He believes shoplifting has grown since the Dunmere bus interchange opened beside the car park on 16 February. Door-counter footfall averaged 14,100 visits a week in Q1, 15,200 in Q2 and 15,900 in Q3. He cites recorded shoplifting incidents in the store log: 6 in Q1, 11 in Q2 and 15 in Q3, mostly razors, cosmetics and batteries. 'My team is logging more than they ever have. We need a guard on the door.' Asked whether staff theft could be involved, he said he trusts his team and pointed to the ethics-line case being closed.
20	E3 [stage S1] Ethics-line case 26-0871 and asset protection follow-up (log): Received 21 Aug, anonymous caller: 'The night stocker at Dunmere [name redacted] keeps taking boxes out the back door after close. Saw it on the 12th and the 19th.' Follow-up by AP investigator R. Okafor, 2 Sep: Reviewed rear-door and dock CCTV for 12 and 19 August, 22:00–06:00. On both nights the named stocker made two trips through the rear door carrying flattened cardboard bales to the compactor, as listed on the closing checklist. No merchandise or sealed cartons seen leaving. Night supervisor confirms bale runs are assigned to this employee. Case closed: unsubstantiated.
21	E4 [stage S1] Store 14 interim shrink report, Q1–Q3 FY2026 (financial-record): Shrink as % of department sales, Q1 / Q2 / Q3. Grocery 0.8 / 1.1 / 1.3. Fresh 1.6 / 2.0 / 2.4. Health & beauty 2.9 / 3.6 / 4.4. General merchandise 2.0 / 2.5 / 3.1. Store total 1.5 / 1.9 / 2.3. Each department's share of store sales stayed within one point across all three quarters: grocery 46%, fresh 24%, health & beauty 14%, general merchandise 16%. Footnote: Q1–Q3 figures are interim estimates extrapolated from rotating department cycle counts. The annual full physical count, carried out by the independent count contractor, is scheduled for 7 December.
22	E5 [stage S1] Email from Bram Castellane, Regional Operations Manager, 6 Nov (manager-account): Re: December count, store 14. Given holiday staffing pressure, I propose we take store 14 out of the 7 December full physical count and roll forward the Q3 book figure for year-end. We already know where that store's number is heading, and the count costs about 140 staff hours plus contractor fees. The other 37 stores would count as planned. Please confirm by 20 November so the contractor can re-plan its schedule.
23	CATALOGUE (full contents)
24	C1 [stage S1] Store 14 staff roster and turnover summary, January–September FY2026 - HR information system extract (system-record): HR extract, store 14, Jan–Sep FY2026. Headcount ranged from 58 to 61. Leavers 9, starters 11 (annualised turnover 31%; chain median 34%). Night replenishment crew: five staff, unchanged since October FY2025 apart from one replacement on 11 May. The assistant store manager changed on 7 July (internal transfer). No disciplinary cases were opened at the store in the period. Two staff were on long-term leave during Q2.
25	C2 [stage S1] Self-checkout vendor briefing on shrink outcomes at client retailers - Slide notes from the self-checkout vendor's account manager, 30 Oct (vendor-account): 'Across our retail clients, stores in their first year of self-checkout typically see shrink 0.3–0.5 points higher than before installation, falling back as attendants gain experience. Our VisionAssist camera upgrade cuts unscanned-item loss by up to 40% and can be installed at Dunmere within three weeks for all four lanes. We recommend Marrowby prioritise store 14 given its Q3 shrink figure.' No client names or underlying data were provided with the slides.
26	C3 [stage S1] Interim shrink by SKU class, store 14, Q3 versus Q1 FY2026 - Finance inventory analytics extract (financial-record): The $23,800 increase in interim shrink dollars between Q1 and Q3 is spread across 61 of 74 SKU classes. Largest contributors: razor blades $1,900, cosmetics $1,600, batteries $1,100, pet food $1,000, canned fish $900, small kitchenware $800. The top ten classes account for 41% of the increase. Fresh produce and bakery together account for 14%. Analyst note: per-class interim figures carry wider error than the store total and should not be read in isolation.
27	C4 [stage S1] Police calls for service coded retail theft, Dunmere district, Q4 FY2025–Q3 FY2026 - Dunmere police district open-data portal (external-data): Calls for service coded 'retail theft', all premises in the district: Q4 FY2025 43, Q1 FY2026 41, Q2 47, Q3 44. Of these, calls from Marrowby store 14: 2, 1, 3, 2. The district covers 23 retail premises. A note on the portal says most low-value shoplifting is not reported to police by retailers, so call counts are a partial measure of retail theft.
28	C5 [stage S1] Front-end equipment change and service records, store 14, March–September FY2026 - Facilities ticketing extract and vendor monthly summary (change-record): 17 Mar: four self-checkout lanes commissioned; go-live 09:00. 2 Apr: all four lanes taken out of service after the payment terminals failed card-scheme recertification (terminal batch PT-7, affecting store 14 only); lanes coned off, screens powered down. Tickets 4471, 4502 and 4590: replacement terminals back-ordered. 26 Jun: replacement terminals installed and certified; lanes back in service on 27 Jun. Vendor monthly summary, Q3: self-checkout handled 18% of store 14 transactions; 412 unscanned-item interventions, or 28.6 per 1,000 self-checkout transactions. Median across the 12 Marrowby stores with self-checkout: 30.4 (range 21–41).
29	C6 [stage S1] Interview with store 14 front-end supervisor - Interview notes, front-end supervisor L. Ferreira-Holm, 5 Nov (staff-account): Ferreira-Holm transferred to store 14 from store 22 on 14 July. 'The self-checkout attendant gets pulled onto tills at peak, so the lanes are unwatched maybe an hour a day. I catch a skip-scan about twice a week, usually low-value stuff. I don't think it's worse than other stores I've worked in. What worries me more is the health and beauty aisle by the entrance; you can't see it from the front end.' She has not reviewed the store's shrink reports.
30	C7 [stage S1] Receiving dock delivery discrepancy log, store 14, Q1–Q3 FY2026 - Store receiving system (log): Deliveries received: 318. Blind-checked (10% sample): 33. Shortages logged on 9 deliveries, totalling $2,140 at cost (0.2% of received value; chain 0.2%). Over-deliveries logged: 4. The distribution centre credited all discrepancies within 30 days. No change in receiving staff or procedure was recorded during the period.
31	C8 [stage S1] Store 14 Q3 business review presentation - Slides presented by store manager D. Pask to regional leadership, 15 Oct (document): Q3 sales $2.81m, up 6% year on year, credited to interchange footfall. Shrink slide headline: 'Up two quarters: external theft wave.' Includes undated photos of empty razor peg hooks. Requests: one contract guard, spider-wrap tags for razors and cosmetics, and a convex mirror for the health and beauty aisle. Labour hours on plan. Customer satisfaction score 82 (chain 80). No shrink analysis beyond the interim totals is presented.
32	C9 [stage S1] CCTV maintenance and camera coverage record, store 14, FY2026 - Security systems contractor service record (system-record): 32 cameras; recorder retention 31 days. Faults: camera 17 (health and beauty aisle) offline 6–19 May, repaired; camera 4 (rear door) lens cleaned 2 August. Coverage audit, June: the end of the health and beauty aisle nearest the entrance was partly blocked by a seasonal display; the display was moved on 1 July. No other faults logged.
33	C10 [stage S1] Asset protection analytics memo on interim shrink estimation and incident reporting, all stores, FY2023–FY2026 - AP Analytics methods note, 28 Oct, circulated to finance (document): 1) Interim quarterly shrink is extrapolated from rotating department cycle counts covering about a fifth of SKUs per quarter. Back-tested against year-end full counts for FY2023–FY2025, the 90% interval for a store of store 14's size is roughly ±0.6 points per quarter. Doubling cycle-count frequency narrows this only to about ±0.5. 2) Across 114 store-years, 27 showed two consecutive interim rises totalling 0.7 points or more; the year-end full count confirmed 13 and did not confirm 14. No store characteristic we tested predicted which. 3) The IR-Mobile incident app launched chain-wide on 1 April. Mean recorded shoplifting incidents per store: Q1 7.1, Q2 12.4, Q3 13.0 (store range 4–31), while chain shrink stayed at 1.6%. Store 14 full-count shrink: FY2023 1.6%, FY2024 1.8%, FY2025 1.5%.
34	C11 [stage S1] Anonymous staff pulse survey results, store 14, June FY2026 - HR pulse survey report (anonymous-staff-survey): Responses: 26 of 59 staff (44%). Engagement 3.6/5 (chain 3.7). 'I feel safe at work' 3.4 (chain 3.6). Selected free-text comments: 'Nights are short-staffed and rushed.' 'Some people take liberties with the staff discount.' 'More shoplifters since the bus station opened.' 'Management doesn't listen about the self-checkouts.' Comments are unverified and cannot be traced to departments or shifts.
35	C12 [stage S1] POS markdown and price-change log, store 14, Q1–Q3 FY2026 - Point-of-sale system report (system-record): Markdowns as a share of sales: 1.1% / 1.0% / 1.2% (chain 1.1% each quarter). Shelf-price changes processed after their effective date: 3.2% / 2.9% / 3.0% of changes (chain 3.1%). No markdown categories were added or removed during the period, and the markdown approval workflow did not change.
36	C13 [stage S1] Interim shrink at neighbouring stores 9 and 22, Q1–Q3 FY2026 - Finance interim shrink report extract (financial-record): Interim shrink, % of sales, Q1 / Q2 / Q3. Store 9 (Calder Rise): 1.4 / 1.3 / 1.6. Store 22 (Westfold): 1.9 / 1.7 / 1.5. Both stores are within 12 miles of store 14 and of similar size. Neither has self-checkout lanes, and neither is near a new transport link. Figures are interim estimates on the same cycle-count basis as store 14.
37	C14 [stage S1] Asset protection close-out report, store 31, FY2025 - AP case close-out report, store 31 (Haverleigh) (prior-report): Interim shrink at store 31 rose from 1.7% to 2.6% over Q2–Q3 FY2025. CCTV review and two apprehensions identified a group stealing razor blades and electric toothbrushes to order. A contract guard and locking peg hooks were installed in October. The year-end full count confirmed shrink of 2.4%, and FY2026 interim shrink at store 31 has run at 1.8%.
38	C15 [stage S1] Dunmere council transport update and community safety minutes, FY2026 - Dunmere borough council published papers, September (external-data): The bus interchange next to the retail park opened on 16 February and averages about 3,200 boardings a day. Community safety minutes for June and September record no change in reported anti-social behaviour around the retail park compared with FY2025. One councillor notes 'anecdotal concerns from traders' about shoplifting, but no figures were presented.
39	CANDIDATES
40	H1: The rise reflects an increase in shoplifting by customers at store 14.
41	H2: The rise reflects an increase in theft by store 14 employees.
42	H3: The self-checkout lanes that went live in March caused the rise.
43	H4: The rise reflects imprecision in the store's interim inventory estimates rather than a change in actual losses.
44	H5: The rise reflects a shift in store 14's sales mix toward higher-shrink departments.
45	R1: Self-checkout go-live at store 14 (17 March) -> Rise in store 14's reported shrink, Q2–Q3 (causes)
46	R2: Increase in store footfall after the bus interchange opened (16 February) -> Rise in store 14's reported shrink, Q2–Q3 (causes)
47	R3: Night stocker's trips through the rear door on 12 and 19 August (as reported in the ethics-line tip) -> Merchandise loss at store 14 (causes)
48	A1: Keep store 14 in the 7 December full physical count by the independent contractor, and hold off on store-specific loss-prevention spending or personnel action until the full-count result has been compared with the interim figures.
49	A2: Contract a full-time security guard for store 14's entrance for the next two quarters.
50	A3: Suspend the night stocker named in the ethics-line tip without pay pending a further investigation.
51	A4: Have store 14 department leads double the frequency of cycle counts in all departments until the December count.
52	A5: Drop store 14 from the December full count and roll forward the Q3 book figure for year-end, as Regional Operations proposes.
53	SCORED ITEMS
54	S1: hypothesis H1 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
55	S2: hypothesis H2 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
56	S3: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
57	S4: hypothesis H4 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
58	S5: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]
59	S6: edge R1 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
60	S7: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
61	S8: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
62	S9: action A1 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
63	S10: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
64	S11: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
65	S12: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
66	S13: action A5 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
67	S14: sufficiency SUFF allowed=[sufficient, insufficient]

answers.justification: Footfall did rise (E2), but the jump in logged incidents lines up with the chain-wide IR-Mobile app launch (C10). Police calls are flat (C4), the council saw no change (C15), and the loss is spread thinly across 61 of 74 SKU classes (C3), so customer theft is possible but not shown.
The only specific allegation was disproved on CCTV (E3), and turnover and the night crew were stable (C1), but nothing excludes employee theft; the discount comment in C11 is unverified.

The lanes were out of service from 2 April to 26 June, yet shrink still rose in Q2 (C5, E4); store 14's Q3 skip-scan rate of 28.6 per 1,000 is below the chain median of 30.4 (C5), and the front-end supervisor sees nothing unusual (C6).

Interim figures have a ±0.6-point error band per quarter, and only 13 of 27 similar two-quarter rises were confirmed by the year-end count, with no store trait predicting which (C10, E4). The rise is about as likely to be noise as real loss.
Each department's share of sales stayed within one point, and shrink rose inside every department (E4).
Q2 shrink rose while the lanes were switched off for almost the whole quarter, and the skip-scan rate is below the chain median (C5, E4).

Footfall and reported shrink rose together after 16 February (E2, E4), but no mechanism is shown: police calls are flat (C4), the council saw no change (C15), the incident rise has an app explanation (C10), and the shrink rise may itself be estimation noise.
CCTV for both nights showed the stocker carrying only cardboard bales to the compactor, which was an assigned duty on the closing checklist (E3).
The independent full count is the only thing that can tell real loss from interim noise (C10, E4), and holding off on spending avoids acting on a reading that is right only about half the time (C10).
A guard would make sense only if customer theft (H1) were confirmed, which it is not (C4, C10, C15); the store 31 precedent (C14) followed apprehensions and CCTV evidence, which store 14 lacks.
The tip was already investigated and found unsubstantiated on CCTV (E3), so suspending the stocker without pay would punish someone with no evidence against them.
Doubling cycle counts is harmless but adds little: it narrows the error band only from ±0.6 to ±0.5 (C10), uses store staff rather than an independent counter, and the full count is weeks away.
Dropping the count would remove the one measurement that can confirm or refute the rise (C10) and would book a figure that may be noise for year-end (E4, E5).

No cause can be singled out: H1, H2 and H4 are all still live (C10, C4, E3), so committing to any substantive loss-prevention or personnel action is not yet justified until the December full count is in.
